fdm_opt_short/diagnosis.json.scope: Independent diagnostic experiments only. These are not accepted training labels. Final seven-run comparison is in final_short.json.
findings: All four invalid baseline IVs in the two short high-correlation cases came from negative OTM prices on the coarse 200x100 spatial grid. Base and fine prices were finite and positive.
Refining X alone or Y alone did not remove the short positive-rho first-wing failure on the other coarse axis; both axes contribute.
Moving the X or Y focus inward or outward shifts errors between strikes. No tested focus change uniformly improves the three difficult short positive-rho strikes.

Reducing short X half-width from 8 to 0.5 improves spatial resolution at fixed interval count. However, a further reduction to 0.125 is rejected: a preserved-spacing expansion past0.25 shifts the first-wing IV by about0.3136bp, above the0.1bp domain tolerance.
No clipping, Richardson acceptance, threshold relaxation, or floating-mode changes were adopted.

A correctly enabled exponential-drift-fit control on the negative-rho random case at200x100 changes the last IV by +0.8206bp, versus the original coarse-to-base shift of307.37bp. It is a different, smaller effect than the main spatial tail error.
